title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff ordering & regional failover load-shedding
author: Priya Ramanathan
description:
Context: We observed a production incident where the SLO enforcer's backoff ordering could be applied out-of-order during high contention, which caused nodes in a stressed region to trigger circuit-breaker fallbacks and immediate regional failover thrashing. That in turn caused aggressive load-shedding and cascading errors for in-flight requests. This PR is an urgent hotfix to stabilize ordering and introduce additional hysteresis to prevent oscillation.

What this PR does: 1) Enforcer ordering: ensure backoff timers and retry tokens are queued and processed by monotonic enqueue timestamp to guarantee deterministic backoff ordering under concurrency. 2) Atomic transitions: fix a race in circuit_breaker.go where state transitions could interleave and cause duplicate fallback triggers; replaced with a single CAS-protected state transition and clearer observability. 3) Hysteresis smoothing: add a configurable hysteresis window (default 30s) before re-adding a previously-failed region to the routing pool to reduce thrash. 4) Load-shedding backoff caps: clamp exponential backoff to avoid unbounded grow under hot tails. 5) Metrics & alerts: emit slo.enforcer.ordering_reorder and slo.enforcer.hysteresis_skipped counters and a debug gauge for last_transition_epoch to help on-call triage. 6) Tests: new unit tests covering ordering, atomic transition, and an integration test simulating a regional outage with concurrent rejoin attempts. 7) Config & rollout: gated behind feature flag feature.slo_enforcer_stable_ordering; rollout to canary clusters first. Includes a short rollback path if needed.

Checklist: - [x] Add deterministic ordering to enforcer queue - [x] Fix atomic CB state transition - [x] Add hysteresis config and documentation - [x] Add unit + integration tests - [x] Add metrics and dashboards snippets - [x] Gate behind feature flag

Notes on risk and rollout: This is a small-surface hotfix: core changes are concentrated in service/slo/enforcer.go and service/slo/circuit_breaker.go. Changes are feature-flagged and backward compatible. We will enable the flag in 3 canary clusters for 1 hour, watch slo.enforcer.* metrics and the canary e2e, then ramp if stable. If we see increased 5xx/overt shedding, the flag can be turned off immediately.

Related: ENG-2245 tracked the incident; SUP-4392 is the support ticket reporting customer impact.
